data.name: Jeff Behrends
data.title: Associate Senior Lecturer in Philosophy
data.short_bio: Jeff Behrends is Associate Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at Harvard University, and the Director of Ethics and Technology Initiatives at the Edmond J. Safra Center for Ethics. He specializes in meta-normativity and the ethics of AI.

data.organization: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST)
data.name: Jerry John Kponyo
data.title: Co-Founder, RAIN Africa; Associate Professor of Telecommunication Engineering
data.bio:
He is currently the Deputy Project Lead of the KNUST Engineering Education Project (KEEP), a 5.5 Million Dollar Africa Center of Excellence (ACE) Impact project sponsored by the World Bank with a focus on Digital Development and Energy. He is a Co-Founder of the Responsible AI Network (RAIN) Africa, which is a collaborative effort between KNUST and TUM Germany. Between 2016 and 2019 he was a visiting lecturer at ESIGELEC, France on a staff mobility programme where he taught postgraduate courses in Business Intelligence and conducted research with staff of ESIGELEC. He has done extensive research in IoT, intelligent systems and AI and currently leads the Emerging Networks and Technologies Research Laboratory at the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, KNUST which focuses on digital development technologies research.

Prof Kponyo’s PhD research focused on applying AI to solving a traffic problem in Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs). He has published over 50 articles in refereed Journals and Conference proceedings. His research focuses on applying intelligent systems and computer models in the area of wireless communication to solve real-life problems. He has done research on applying artificial intelligence to Vehicular Ad hoc Networks, where knowledge of the behaviour of ants as they search for food is applied to solve a traffic problem. In the area of information dissemination in Vehicular Networks, he has developed a Minimum Spanning Tree clustering algorithm which substantially reduces the traffic overhead as far as information sharing in vehicles is concerned. He has worked on an emergency call routing scheme for disaster management in which he proposes an algorithm which gives priority to distressed calls from emergency situations and as a result reducing the response time in emergency situations. In the area of wireless communication, he has worked on the development of circularly polarized slot antennas for multiband applications. Together with other collaborators, he has worked on the possibility of using the orbital angular momentum of the EM wave for information transmission. The preliminary results have shown this to be possible and this has the potential of solving the problem of bandwidth limitation in the wireless band. His current works include precision agriculture using IoT, applying the Internet of Things (IoT) and Light Fidelity (LiFi) to Vehicular Networks as well as IoT security.

He has served on the Technical Planning Committee of many Internal Conferences and is reviewer for many reputable Journals in his field of expertise. He also leads the KNUST College of Engineering Innovation Center which drives innovation among students. For the past four years the Center has hosted students and staff of Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), South Korea who have collaborated with students of KNUST to develop working prototypes. Prior to becoming the Dean of Faculty he was the Head of Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department at KNUST. He is also the KNUST focal person on the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN organization headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

Professor Kponyo is a member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers and the Ghana Institution of Engineers. He is also a mentor and a Research Advisor of the Africa Research Academy for Women.
data.short_bio: Prof. Jerry John Kponyo is the Head of the Quality Assurance and Planning Unit of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) under the Vice-Chancellor’s Office. He is the former Dean of the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, KNUST. He is a certified Project Management Professional and has significant experience in managing funded projects and international collaborations.

data.name: Jessica Eynard
data.title: Associate Professor in Law
data.bio:
Since 2019, she has served as co-director of the Master of Law, Digital, AI at the University of Toulouse Capitole. In addition, Jessica is a member of the chair in Law, Accountability and Social Trust in AI of the Artificial Intelligence Institute of Toulouse (ANITI). In 2012, she received the thesis award from the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL) for her thesis on the notion of personal data, published by Michalon.

Jessica has also directed the publication of a collective work on digital identity, published by Larcier in 2020, which received an award from the International Forum of Cybersecurity in 2021. She is currently co-editing two books: one on artificial intelligence (co-edited with Céline Castets-Renard, Professor at the University of Ottawa) and the other on self-sovereign digital identity (co-edited with Giorgia Macilotti, Researcher at the University of Toulouse Capitole).
data.short_bio: Jessica Eynard is an Assistant Professor at the University of Toulouse Capitole in France. Her research interests include artificial intelligence law, digital identity and personal data protection law.

data.name: Jibu Elias
data.title: Content and Research Head
data.bio: Jibu is also a member of the OECD Network of Experts on AI (ONE AI) and one of the founding Editorial Board Members of Springer’s AI and Ethics journal, the first multidisciplinary academic journal on AI ethics. With years of experience covering emerging technologies with PC Mag and the Times of India Group, Jibu’s work currently focuses on building a unified AI ecosystem in India. He is an alumnus of The London School of Economics, where he studied International Relations, specializing in Sino-India relations.
data.short_bio: Jibu Elias is an AI Ethicist, Researcher, and the leading expert on India’s AI ecosystem and is the Research & Content Lead at INDIAai -The National AI Portal for the Government of India.

data.name: John Basl
data.title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
data.short_bio: John Basl is an Associate Professor of Philosophy in the Department of Philosophy & Religion at Northeastern University, and a researcher at the Northeastern Ethics Institute. He works primarily in moral philosophy and applied ethics, especially on issues related to emerging technologies.

data.name: José Luis Fernández Fernández
data.title: Professor
data.bio:
From 2000 to 2003, he was Vice-Rector of External Relations and University Extension at the Comillas Pontifical University. For eleven years, he was Coordinator of Ethics of the Professions at the Universidad Pontificia Comillas ICAI-ICADE and General Coordinator of the Unijes Group of Ethics of the Professions. He has completed the CESCOM Compliance Certificate and is an accredited member of the ICCP, International Federation of Compliance Associations (IFCA).

José Luis is also a Fellow of the Caux Round Table, and the Chairman of the Ethics and Social Responsibility Subcommittee (CTN 165 SC2) of the Spanish Association for Standardization (UNE). He was President of EBEN-Spain between 1993 and 2007. He has written several books and numerous articles on the ethical aspects of digitalization (Business Digital Ethics). José Luis holds a Doctorate in Philosophy (PhD) from the Faculty of Philosophy of the Universidad Pontificia Comillas and an MBA from ICADE.
data.short_bio: José Luis Fernández Fernández is a Professor at the Faculty of Economic and Business Sciences (ICADE) and Director of the Iberdrola Chair of Economic and Business Ethics.

data.name: Kan Suzuki
data.title: Professor
data.bio: After serving at the Ministry of International Trade and Industry and at Keio University, Kan Suzuki assumed the post of State Minister of MEXT during his twelve-year career at the House of Councillors. His recent assignments include Professor the University of Tokyo and Keio University under the cross appointment system (2014 - present), Special advisor to MEXT (2015-present).
data.short_bio: Kan Suzuki is a Professor at the Graduate School of Public Policy, University of Tokyo Professor as well as at the Graduate School Media and government, Keio University. He is also the special advisor to the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT).

data.name: Kelly Bronson
data.title: Canada Research Chair in Science & Society
data.bio: Kelly has published her work in national (Canadian Journal of Communication) and international journals (Science as Culture, Journal of Responsible Innovation, Big Data and Society). She has recently published a book on big data and AI in agriculture with McGill-Queen’s University Press titled, Immaculate Conception of Data: Agribusiness, activists and their shared politics of the future.
data.short_bio: Kelly Bronson is a Canada Research Chair in Science & Society at University of Ottawa in Canada. She is a social scientist studying the societal and ethical dimensions of controversial technologies and their governance—from GMOs to big data and AI

data.name: Ken Ito
data.title: Professor of Music, Brain Cognitive Information Philosophy and Ethics at the University of Tokyo
data.bio:
Born in Tokyo, Itoken studied composition and piano under Teizo Matsumura, Yoritsume Matsudaira, Yuji Takahashi and Luigi Nono, and received prizes with the Judgement (judgement?) of György Ligeti, Luciano Berio and Henri Dutilleux. He also studied conducting under Tsunesada Tachibana and Leonard Bernstein.

 He earned a M.A. in Solid State Physics, and a Ph.D. in Fundamentals of Music from the University of Tokyo University, where his research focused on an interdisciplinary work of music, physical and brain cognitive science.

Since 1999, he has been working as a professor of composition, conducting and fundamental informatics at the University of Tokyo, while his research interest includes Ethical aspect of media and information.

As a composer and theoretician, Professor Ito has solved Arnold Schönberg's three problems (Polyphony, Klangfarbenmelodie and space music cognition, Sprechgesang) with Nono. As a conductor he has established "Spectral conducting" method "without figure" with Pierre Boulez. Furthermore, he has started brain cognitive research on "Space music("Raummusik") at first with Karlheinz Stockhausen. Later on with Wolfgang Wagner and Eva Wagner=Pasquier, Professor Ito worked on dynamical space-time characteristics of BAYREUTHER FESTSPIELHAUS designed by Richard Wagner for his huge Space-Time "Musikdrama <Der Ring des Nibelungen>".

One of his undergraduate friends Professor Ito studied Physics together at the University of Tokyo was involved in the sarin gas attack on a Tokyo subway in 1995 – the attack that was just one of a series of criminal activities including murder, kidnapping, extortion, and the illegal manufacture of arms and drugs carried out by the new religious movement, Aum Shinrikyo. His friend was one of the perpetrators of this crime. Professor Ito immediately started ethical study based on physical and brain cognitive science. This activity is well known in Japan and received the Kaiko-Ken Award in 2006. Professor Ito also supported his friend throughout his trials and during the detention after the sentence of death penalty, up to the last day and after that.

Last but not least, he organized and played cross-disciplinary projects and performances between music and basic sciences at National University of RWANDA(2006-08), high schools in FUKUSHIMA, and, more recently, online classes and performances due to COVID-19 .

Artistic Director of “Raummusik Kollegium Berlin”, President of JASTICE : Japan Association of Space and Time Composition and Enterprises and founding member of Global AI Ethics Consortium.

Works:

Cosmostroph(1993)

Quand-Temps---"No-Opera" after M.Duchamp and J. Cage(1998)

Electric Hungarian Hoquetus based on twin prime numbers, epitaph for György Ligeti (2006),

"<Voyelles> unthreaded, Rimbaud"(2015)

The Voyage of Prince Takaoka(1991-/2020-).

 

Performances:

World first performance: The Tale of Genji (Yoritsune MATSUDAIRA)(1995)

Japanese first Performance: OCEAN (John Cage, posthumous work with

New York Merce Cunningham Danse Company. )(1998)

Japanese first no-cut performance: Tristan and Isolde (Richard WAGNER) (2013)

Beethoven 250 COVID to CUPID Global network project (2020)
data.short_bio: Ken Ito is a Japanese Composer and Professor of Music, Brain Cognitive Information Philsophy and Ethics and the University of Tokyo.

data.organization: African Center for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technology
data.name: Maha Jouini
data.title: Founder
data.bio:
Maha is a prominent advocate for youth and women’s rights, fighting against racism and gender-based violence. In 2018, Maghreb Voices named her their Personality of the Year for her work championing women’s rights. She is an author and blogger, using her platform to defend human rights in the MENA region. She has also published several articles on AI policies and the future of work in Africa. 

Maha is pursuing a PhD in Computer Science and Data Science. She holds a master’s degree in AI and emerging technologies from the Tianjin University of Education and Technology in China, where she spent many years living and working.
data.short_bio: Maha Jouini is an expert in AI and emerging technologies based in Mauritania. She founded the African Center for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Technology in 2022 to support the adoption of AI policies across the African continent. Maha is a member of the Center for AI and Digital Policy’s (CAIDP) Fall 2022 AI Policy Clinic Research Group. She has also served as the North Africa Regional Director for the Africa Chamber of Digital Commerce since 2020, and was recently appointed an Ambassador for Cluster Digital Africa.

data.name: Maria Luciana Axente
data.title: Responsible AI Lead
data.bio: Maria is a member of various Advisory Boards - UK All-Party Parliamentary Group on AI (APPG AI) ,ORBIT and; SKEMA AI Institute, Vice Chair of techUK Data and AI leadership committee and member of BSI/ISO and; IEEE AI standard groups. She is also a passionate advocate for children rights in the age of AI, serving as member of the Advisory Board for UNICEF #AI4Children and World Economic Forum Generation AI programmes. At PwC, Maria manages the company’s efforts in deploying responsible AI and data across the UK business, its operations and clients.
data.short_bio: Maria is a globally recognised, award winning AI ethics expert, public policy contributor.

data.name: Mark Findlay
data.title: Professorial Research Fellow, Director, Centre for AI and Data Governance
data.bio: In addition, he has honorary Chairs at the Australian National University, the University of Edinburgh and the University of New South Wales, an Honorary Senior Research Fellow at the British Institute for International and Comparative Law, and an Honorary Fellow of the Law School, University of Edinburgh.
data.short_bio: Professor Mark Findlay is a Professor of Law at Singapore Management University, and Director of its Centre for AI and Data Governance, where he is a Professorial Research Fellow.

data.name: Marta Galceran
data.title: Research Fellow - Global Cities Programme
data.bio: Marta also leads the research at the Global Observatory of Urban Artificial Intelligence (GOUAI), within the Cities Coalition for Digital Rights. Before joining CIDOB, she held the position of Program Coordinator of the Smart City Expo World Congress and senior consultant at Anteverti, where she advised local governments and international organizations (i.e., UN-Habitat, IADB, European Commission) on internationalization and urban innovation policies. Marta holds an MA in International Relations from the University of Warwick and a BA in Political Sciences from Pompeu Fabra University.
data.short_bio: Marta Galceran is a Research Fellow with the Global Cities Programme at CIDOB (Barcelona Centre for International Affairs), and a part-time lecturer on International Relations at Pompeu Fabra University and CEI-International Affairs. Her research focuses on city diplomacy, urban alliances and global governance, particularly in the field of digital transitions and technological humanism. She has authored several policy papers, academic articles, and other publications on these topics.

data.name: Maui Hudson
data.title: Associate Professor and Director, Te Kotahi Research Institute
data.bio: Access to data and governance of data are key issues emerging from his research and led to his involvement in the establishment of Te Mana Raraunga, the Māori Data Sovereignty Network, and the Global Indigenous Data Alliance. He is the Co-Director of ENRICH, a collaboration between NYU and University of Waikato, and a Co-Director of Local Contexts, a system which digitally tags Indigenous interests in traditional knowledge and biodata.
data.short_bio: Maui affiliates to Te Whakatohea, Nga Ruahine, and Te Mahurehure iwi and is currently the deputy chair of the Whakatohea Māori Trust Board. Maui is an Associate Professor and Director of the Te Kotahi Research Institute at the University of Waikato. His research is interdisciplinary in nature focusing on the application of mātauranga Māori (indigenous knowledge) to decision-making across a range of contexts from new technologies to health, the environment to innovation.

data.organization: University of Lyon, Faculty of Dentistry
data.name: Maxime Ducret
data.title: Dentist and Associate Professor
data.short_bio: Maxime Ducret is a dentist and associate professor in Prosthetics and Digital Dentistry at the University of Lyon. He also serves as a Hospital Practitioner at the University Hospital of Lyon.

data.organization: Maat for Peace, Development and Human Rights
data.name: Muhammad Mokhtar
data.title: Deputy Director of Democracy and Good Governance Unit
data.bio: Muhammad is a human rights activist and an expert in political technology. His work focuses on investigating, analyzing and advocating against human rights abuse linked to governments and international organizations. His goal is to end human rights abuses, especially in the Middle East, and to develop online rights mediating the relationship between humans and technology.
data.short_bio: Muhammad Mokhtar is the Deputy Director of the Democracy and Good Governance Unit at Maat for Peace, Development and Human Rights.

data.name: Nagla Rizk
data.title: Professor of Economics
data.bio:
Nagla’s area of research, teaching and advocacy is the economics of knowledge, technology and development, with focus on governance of data, responsible Artificial Intelligence, fair work in the platform economy, innovation, gender and inclusion in Egypt, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). In her work as founding director of the Access to Knowledge for Development Center (A2K4D), Nagla is engaged with regional and international partners working on policy-oriented research that focuses on the developmental perspective of knowledge in general and knowledge governance in particular. 

Nagla also founded the Open Data for Development Node for the Middle East and North Africa. She leads the Feminist AI Research (f<a+i>r) network’s MENA hub, Open African Innovation Research Partnership (Open AIR)’s North Africa hub, and the Fairwork Egypt team, in partnership with Oxford Internet Institute. She is a Faculty Associate at Harvard’s Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society, Affiliate Faculty at Harvard Law School’s CopyrightX course and an Affiliated Fellow of Yale Law School’s Information Society Project. She is an Associate Member at the University of Ottawa’s Centre for Law, Technology and Society.
data.short_bio: Nagla Rizk is a Professor of Economics at The American University in Cairo, as well as the Founding Director of the Access to Knowledge for Development Center (A2K4D).

data.name: Natalia Domagala
data.title: Head of Data Ethics
data.bio: She previously advised on open government and open data policies for the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport in the UK, and implemented open data challenges for 360Giving. She has research experience in anthropology, gender, civic tech, and economic development, and she has recently co-edited a book: Situating Open Data: Global Trends in Local Contexts. Natalia is a Policy Fellow at the Centre for Science and Policy, University of Cambridge. She received her MSc in Local Economic Development from the London School of Economics and Political Science and her BA in Anthropology and Media from Goldsmiths, University of London.
data.short_bio: Natalia Domagala leads on data ethics policy at the Central Digital and Data Office, Cabinet Office in the UK.

data.name: Nicole Gillespie
data.title: KPMG Chair in Organisational Trust & Professor in Management & KPMG Chair in Trust School of Business
data.bio:
Trained as an organizational psychologist, Nicole’s research focuses on trust development and repair in organisational contexts, and in contexts where trust is challenged (e.g. after a trust failure, in complex stakeholder environments, during organizational transformation and digital disruption, in emerging technologies and virtual healthcare, in cross-cultural relations). Current research projects focus on understanding stakeholder trust in organizations and industries, organizational trust repair, designing trustworthy organizations, trust in Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies, and stakeholder trust and uptake of telemedicine. Her research appears in leading international journals, including the Academy of Management Review, Journal of Management, Journal of Applied Psychology, Organization Studies, Accounting Organizations and Society, European Journal of Information Systems, Journal of Services Research, Business Ethics Quarterly, Journal of Business Ethics, Human Resource Management, Sloan Management Review and Work and Stress, as well as in books and book chapters. She has also published in a range of health journals including Lancet Digital Health, Journal of Telemedicine and Telecare, Digital Health, and Dermatology. Her work has been extensively presented in Europe, the USA and Australia. She is Deputy Editor of the Journal of Trust Research and on the editorial board of the leading leadership journal, Leadership Quarterly.

Nicole has written commissioned research reports and case studies on building and repairing stakeholder trust for the UK Institute of Business Ethics, the World Economic Forum, and a policy note for the UK Parliament on restoring trust in the financial sector after the global financial crisis. Her most recent reports in collaboration with KPMG are Trustworthy by Design: A practical guide to organisational trust ; Trust in Artificial Intelligence: Australian Insights 2020 ; and Achieving Trustworthy AI: A model for trustworthy artificial intelligence. Her research and consulting has led to positive changes in industry, government and policy across a range of sectors, including Health, Resources, Finance and Banking, Higher Education, R&D, Not-for-Profit and the Defence industry. Clients include KPMG, the World Economic Forum, the Ontario Hospital Association, Barclays Bank, UBS Bank, Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital, the Royal Flying Doctor Service, CSIRO, The Australian Army, Bank of Queensland, Santos, Origin Energy and various government agencies. She has attracted over $7million in research funding as a Chief Investigator with her colleagues, including ARC, NHMRC and industry grants. Nicole is an active member of the Academy of Management, the European Group of Organisational Studies, and the First International Network on Trust and sits on multiple Advisory Boards.

Nicole has over twenty years experience in designing and delivering MBA, Executive MBA, specialist masters and undergraduate courses. She is the recipient of five teaching excellence awards and, together with former PhD student Mattia Anesa, two best paper awards from the Academy of Management. She is the recipient of the 2016 UQ Business School Research Award. In 2019 she was made a Fellow of the Australian and New Zealand School of Government in recognition of outstanding contribution to public management.
data.short_bio: Nicole Gillespie is the KPMG Chair in Organizational Trust and Professor of Management at the University of Queensland Business School, and an International Research Fellow at the Centre for Corporate Reputation, Oxford University. She co-leads the Trust, Ethics and Governance Alliance at the University of Queensland. Nicole joined UQ Business School in January 2010. Prior to this she held faculty and research positions at Melbourne Business School, Warwick Business School (UK), The Australian & New Zealand School of Government, The University of Melbourne, University of Queensland, and Swinburne University of Technology.

data.name: Nuria Oliver
data.title: Scientific Director and Co-Founder
data.bio: Nuria is well known for her work in computational models of human behaviour, human computer-interaction, intelligent user interfaces, mobile computing and big data for social good. She is the named inventor of 41 patents, and a frequent keynote speaker both for technical and non-technical audiences. She regularly collaborates with and is featured by the media. She is very passionate about the power of technology to improve our quality of life, both individually and collectively. Nuria invests significant effort in outreach efforts to make technology more accessible to non technical audiences and to inspire young people – especially young women – to pursue careers in technology.
data.short_bio: Nuria is a computer scientist. She holds a Ph.D. from the Media Lab at MIT. She is the first female computer scientist in Spain to be named an ACM Distinguished Scientist and an ACM Fellow. She is also a Fellow of the European Association of Artificial Intelligence and an IEEE Fellow. She is a member of the Academia Europaea and the fourth and youngest female member of the Spanish Royal Academy of Engineering.

data.name: Nydia Remolina
data.title: Adjunct Faculty
data.bio: Nydia Remolina is a lawyer with more than 10 years of experience in the financial services industry and in the academia as a lecturer and researcher. Currently, Nydia is a Research Associate at the SMU Centre for AI and Data Governance and Adjunct Faculty at Singapore Management University. Her main areas of work and academic research include AI and ethics, financial regulation, fintech, and the intersection of law and technology. She has taught or delivered lectures at several institutions in the United States, Asia, Europe, and Latin America. She has been an instructor for the Global Certificate Program jointly organized by the Harvard Law School and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO). She has also been invited to speak about fintech and financial regulation at various international organizations, including the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO), and the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Nydia has also acted as a Senior Advisor to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), she worked at Sullivan & Cromwell´s New York Office and has been an advisor for policy affairs and innovation at financial institutions.
data.short_bio: Nydia Remolina is an Adjunct Faculty at Singapore Management University, and a Research Associate at the SMU Centre for AI and Data Governance.

data.organization: University Center for Human Values, Princeton University
data.name: Peter Singer
data.title: Ira W. DeCamp Professor of Bioethics
data.bio:
Singer first became well-known internationally after the publication of Animal Liberation in 1975. Some of his other well-known books are: Practical Ethics, The Expanding Circle, How Are We to Live?, Rethinking Life and Death, Pushing Time Away, The Life You Can Save, The Point of View of the Universe (co-authored with Katarzyna de Lazari-Radek), Ethics in the Real World, and Why Vegan?  

In 2012, Singer was made a Companion of the Order of Australia, the nation’s highest civic honor.  He founded the charity The Life You Can Save and is a founding co-editor of the Journal of Controversial Ideas. In 2021, he was awarded the Berggruen Prize for Philosophy and Culture.
data.short_bio: Peter Singer was born in Melbourne, Australia, in 1946, and educated at the University of Melbourne and the University of Oxford. After teaching in England, the United States and Australia, he has, since 1999, been Ira W. DeCamp Professor of Bioethics in the University Center for Human Values at Princeton University.

data.name: Piet Naudé
data.title: Professor of Ethics
data.bio: His academic background is in Philosophy and Theology and he specializes in ethics methodology and applied ethics with a global perspective. His most recent book, Contemporary Management Education: Eight questions that will shape its future in the 21st century (Springer 2022) is an ethical perspective on business school education, and includes a dedicated chapter on technology.
data.short_bio: Piet Naudé is immediate past Director and Professor of Ethics at University of Stellenbosch Business School, South Africa.

data.name: Rafael Calvo
data.title: Faculty of Engineering, Dyson School of Design Engineering
data.bio:
Some of his roles include:

  • Director for Research at the Dyson School of Design Engineering.
  • Co-lead (Imperial) at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence.
  • Chief Investigator at Australian Research Hub on Digital Enhanced Living.
  • Associate Investigator at the Australian Centre of Excellence in Autonomous Decision Making.
  • Associate investigator NHMRC Centre of Centre of Research Excellence to Optimise Sleep in Brain Ageing.
  • Ethics Advisory Board, Digital Catapult.
  • Co-Editor of IEEE Transactions on Technology and Society.
data.short_bio: Rafael A. Calvo, PhD is a Professor at Imperial College London focusing on the design of systems that support wellbeing in areas of mental health, medicine and education, and on the ethical challenges raised by new technologies. In 2015 Calvo was appointed a Future Fellow of the Australian Research Council to study the design of wellbeing-supportive technology.

data.name: Ramya Malur Srinivasan
data.title: Senior Research Manager
data.short_bio: Dr. Ramya Malur Srinivasan is a Senior Research Manager with Fujitsu Research, where she is a member of the AI Trust Research Center. Ramya’s background is in the areas of computer vision, machine learning, explainable AI, and AI ethics; with her research spanning diverse applications such as creativity, healthcare and finance.

data.name: Renée Cummings
data.title: Data Activist in Residence
data.bio:
Foreseeing trends and anticipating disruptions, she’s committed to diverse and inclusive AI strategy development; using AI to empower and transform communities and cultures; securing diverse and inclusive participation in the 4IR, helping companies navigate the AI landscape and developing future AI leaders.

A multicultural cross-connector of multiple fields and an innovative collaborator, her passion is forming connections and unifying people and technologies; enhancing quality of life and economic prosperity. She’s also a criminal psychologist, therapeutic jurisprudence and rehabilitation specialist, substance abuse therapist, crisis intelligence, crisis communication and media specialist, creative science communicator and journalist.

She has a solid background in government relations, public affairs, reputation management and litigation PR. A sought after thought-leader, inspirational motivational speaker and mentor, Ms. Cummings is also a Columbia University community scholar.
data.short_bio: Renée Cummings is a New York-based criminologist and international consultant who specializes in Artificial Intelligence (AI); ethical AI, implicit bias in AI, diversity and inclusion in AI, algorithmic authenticity and accountability, data integrity and equity, AI for social good and social justice in AI policy and governance.

data.organization: The Institute for Experiential AI at Northeastern University (Silicon Valley Campus)
data.name: Ricardo Baeza-Yates
data.title: Research Professor
data.bio:
Ricardo Baeza-Yates is currently a Research Professor (half-time) at the Institute for Experiential AI of Northeastern University, Silicon Valley campus, since January 2021. He is also a member of the DATA Lab at the Khoury College of Computer Sciences. The rest of the time, he does consulting for tech startups, companies and non-profit international institutions. Between 2016 and 2020, he was CTO of NTENT, a search technology company based in Carlsbad, California. Previously, he was VP of Research at Yahoo Labs, based in Barcelona, Spain, and later in Sunnyvale, California, from January 2006 to February 2016. Between 2008 and 2012 he also supervised Yahoo Labs Haifa and between 2012 and 2014 Yahoo Labs London. Until 2005, he was the director of the Center for Web Research at the Department of Computer Science of the Engineering School  of the University of Chile; and ICREA Professor and Founder of the Web Science and Social Computing Research Group (formerly Web Research Group) at the Department of Information and Communication Technologies of Universitat Pompeu Fabra in Barcelona, Spain. He maintains ties with both mentioned universities as a part-time professor. Finally, he is also an adjunct professor at the CS department of the University of Waterloo, Canada.  

His research interests include algorithms and data structures, information retrieval, web search and data mining, and data science and visualization.

He is an ACM Fellow and IEEE Fellow.
data.short_bio: Ricardo Baeza-Yates is currently a Research Professor (half-time) at the Institute for Experiential AI of Northeastern University, Silicon Valley campus, since January 2021. His research interests include algorithms and data structures, information retrieval, web search and data mining, and data science and visualization.

data.name: Richard Benjamins
data.title: Co-Founder & VP of OdiseIA, Chief AI & Data Strategist
data.bio: He was Group Chief Data Officer at AXA (Insurance) and before that held for 10 years executive positions at Telefonica on Big Data and Analytics. He is the founder of Telefonica’s Big Data for Social Good department, a member of the B2G data-sharing Expert Group of the EC, and a frequent speaker on Artificial Intelligence events. He holds a PhD in Cognitive Science, has published over 100 scientific articles, and is author of the books “The myth of the algorithm: tales and truths of artificial intelligence” (Spanish) and “A Data-Driven Company” (forthcoming). He is strategic advisor of several start-ups, including BigML and Focus360.
data.short_bio: Dr. Richard Benjamins is Chief AI & Data Strategist at Telefonica. He is among the 100 most influential people in data-driven business (DataIQ 100, 2018). He is also co-founder and Vice President of the Spanish observatory for ethical and social impacts of AI (OdiseIA).

data.name: Serge Abiteboul
data.title: Computer Science Researcher
data.bio: He is known for his many contributions in the areas of finite model theory, database theory, and database systems. In 2008, according to Citeseer, he is the most highly cited researcher in the data management area who works at a European institution. Abiteboul is also known for two books, one on database theory and one on Web data management. He frequently writes for French newspapers, including Le Monde, Libération, and La Tribune. A member of the ARCEP, the independent agency in charge of regulating telecommunications in France, Abiteboul has been an advocate of net neutrality. He has also been critical of virtual assistants and their impact on privacy.
data.short_bio: Serge Abiteboul is a senior researcher at the Institut national de recherche en informatique et en automatique (INRIA), the French national research institute focusing on computer science and related areas, and has been a professor of the Collège de France.

data.name: Shannon Vallor
data.title: Baillie Gifford Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence
data.bio:
Her research explores the philosophy and ethics of emerging science and technologies. Her current research project focuses on the impact of emerging technologies--particularly those involving automation and artificial intelligence--on the moral and intellectual habits, skills and virtues of human beings: our character.

Her work investigates how human character is being transformed by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, new social media, surveillance, and biomedical technologies, and appears in journals such as Ethics and Information Technology, Philosophy & Technology, and Techne, as well as a 2016 book from Oxford University Press:  Technology and the Virtues: A Philosophical Guide to a Future Worth Wanting. She is also the editor of the forthcoming Oxford Handbook of Philosophy of Technology and is currently working on a new book on the subject of artificial intelligence and ethics: The AI Mirror: Rebuilding Humanity in an Age of Machine Thinking.
data.short_bio: Shannon Vallor is the Baillie Gifford Chair in the Ethics of Data and Artificial Intelligence at the University of Edinburgh's Edinburgh Futures Institute, where she is also appointed as Professor in Philosophy.

data.organization: Tilburg Institute for Law, Technology and Society
data.name: Siddharth Peter de Souza
data.title: Postdoctoral Researcher - Global Data Justice Project
data.bio:
Prior to joining TILT, Siddharth was a PhD researcher at the Humboldt University of Berlin. He studied law at the University of Cambridge and the University of Delhi. He previously worked as a German Chancellor Fellow at the Max Planck Foundation for International Peace and Rule of Law, Heidelberg and as a judicial clerk at the High Court of Delhi. 

Siddharth is the founder of Justice Adda, a law and design social venture which develops innovative legal content to make the law accessible, useful and usable in India. He is also the co-founder of d-Van, a design thinking transformations lab based in India.
data.short_bio: Siddharth Peter de Souza is a postdoctoral researcher for the Global Data Justice project at the Tilburg Institute for Law, Technology and Society (TILT). He is interested in the role data plays at the intersection of law and development.

data.name: Smitha Krishna Prasad
data.title: Fritz Family Fellow
data.bio:
Smitha is an Assistant Professor of law (on leave) at the National Law School of India University, Bangalore. She is also a Senior Research Fellow at the Digital Asia Hub, where she is involved in research related to the governance of digital infrastructure used to deliver public services, and more broadly digital platforms.

Smitha holds an LL.M. degree in International Legal Studies from the New York University School of Law, and a B.A.LL.B. from Symbiosis Law School, Pune.
data.short_bio: Smitha is a Fritz Family Fellow with Georgetown’s Tech & Society Program and an SJD Candidate at Georgetown Law. Smitha’s primary research interests focus on issues around digital governance, privacy, data protection and surveillance. She also works on questions of emerging technology and law, and the expansion of tech regulation. Her current research focuses on policy and legal frameworks applicable in relation to the use of digital technologies in government functions and services, and the role that international organisations are playing in this context.

data.name: Sundar Narayanan
data.title: Consultant and Advisor - Ethics and Compliance, Fellow
data.bio:
His primary experiences include advising companies on Ethics, Risk and Compliance frameworks, implementing monitoring mechanisms for risk and compliance, and formulating communication and training approaches to create awareness around organizational ethics and compliance standards. 

Sundar is also a researcher working on technology and data ethics. His research objective is focused on ”Tech Ethics: Culture, Controls and Compliance”. This includes the organizational behavior and cultural influence driving ethics and responsibility in AI development and deployment. He has spoken at forums on topics relating to data monetisation, data ethics and sustainability amongst others. In his spare time, Sundar hosts a successful podcast where he exchanges perspectives with professionals and experts from around the world.
data.short_bio: Sundar Narayanan is an Ethics and Compliance professional with over 15 years of experience in providing advisory services to companies in India, the UAE, Japan, Kenya, Tanzania and Zambia.

data.name: Susan Scott-Parker
data.title: Founder
data.bio:
Her work is grounded in the reality of both business and disability and is distinctive in her determination to deliver practical, tangible mutual benefit for business, people with disabilities, the global economy, and wider society. 

In 2003 Susan invented and launched the concept and language of ‘Disability Confidence’ – knowing that if we can change the way we talk about the world, we make it easier to change the world. She continues to drive innovation by connecting sectors and leaders worldwide who would otherwise rarely meet. Priorities now include harnessing the power of 'disability confident procurement' to drive business improvement and enabling multinationals to deliver consistent best practice in how they provide every employee with the tools and flexibility that they require in order to realise their potential.

Susan also leads: "'How Do You Lip Read a Robot?-  Tackling AI powered Unfair Recruitment:" a community of global thought leaders that includes IBM, Oxford Brooke's University's Institute for Ethical AI; The European Disability Forum; Simmons and Simmons; Bioss International; Face Equality International and the Institute of Intelligent Systems and Robotics IST/UL Portugal

She sits on the Steering Group of the Global Action on Disability Network. GLAD brings together the international development sector including bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations and the International Disability Alliance, to promote disability inclusive development. 
  
Susan has built various long-standing strategic alliances which include: the  Essl Foundation (Vienna) - she is their ZeroProject Global Ambassador; the Australian Network on Disability; G3ICT, the Austrian/German MyAbility business disability network; Community Business (Hong Kong); CCRW (Canada); and PurpleSpace (UK). She advises the ILO's Global Business Disability Network, GIZ (Germany), Inclusion Works led by Sightsavers and supports the Valuable500 campaign.
data.short_bio: Susan Scott-Parker, OBE HonD is internationally recognised as a spirited and creative thought leader on how to mobilise business behind the economic and social inclusion of people with disabilities worldwide. She has made a career from challenging outdated assumptions regarding both disability as it affects business and the potential of responsible business to adapt respectfully for human reality. She focuses on where the needs of business & the aspirations of persons with disabilities coincide.

data.name: Tannya Jajal
data.title: Regional Resource Manager
data.bio: She has spoken at 40+ events to represent her views on future technology, the future of work, and the ethics of artificial intelligence. Tannya encourages current and future leaders to explore the ethical and practical implications of exponential technologies on business, life and society at large. She is an advocate of radical innovation, the rise of meaningful work and skills in a post-automation world, and a proponent of educational reform. Tannya is a Regional Resource Manager at VMware, a market leader in hybrid cloud solutions, leading the way forward for digital transformation.
data.short_bio: Tannya is a keynote speaker, futurist, and author of the upcoming book, "Thinking Machines: A.I. and the Intelligence Explosion".

data.name: Viviana Polisena
data.title: Professor-Researcher
data.bio: Her research interests include artificial intelligence, ethics, logic, philosophy, history and sociology of sciences. She holds a master’s degree in Human and Social Sciences from Paris-Sorbonne University and a diploma in the Philosophy of Physics from the Institute of Philosophy and Complexity Sciences (IFICC) in Chile. She is currently pursuing a doctorate of philosophy at the Pontifical Catholic University of Argentina (UCA). She is a member of the Global AI Ethics Consortium and a Fellowships Evaluation Expert at the European Commission.
data.short_bio: Viviana Polisena is a Professor-Researcher at the Catholic University of Córdoba.

data.organization: Centre for AI and Data Governance, Singapore Management University
data.name: Willow Wong
data.title: Research Associate
data.short_bio: Willow Wong is a research associate at the Centre for AI and Data Governance, Singapore Management University. Her research interests are in moral philosophy, ethics and the philosophy of technology. Willow was recently appointed to the position of Adjunct Faculty at the Yong Pung How School of Law and enjoys teaching AI, Law, and Ethics with Jane Loo.

data.organization: University Center for Human Values, Princeton University
data.name: Yip Fai Tse
data.title: Research Assistant
data.short_bio: Tse Yip Fai is a research assistant for Professor Peter Singer at Princeton University. He is researching the impact and ethics of artificial intelligence on nonhuman animals. Fai holds a degree in Chemistry from the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and one in Banking and Finance from the University of London. He is a 2021 Foresight Fellow in Animal Ethics For Artificial Intelligence. He was previously the China Strategy Consultant for Mercy For Animals, responsible for research and strategy for their expansion plans in China and Asia.

data.name: Yves Poullet
data.title: Co-Chairman of the Namur Digital Institute (NADI), Founder of the CRIDS (1979), Eméritus Professor
data.bio:
He has published more than 400 articles and participated as promoter or member of the jury in more than 40 theses in many countries (France, Norway, UK, Italy, Holland, Canada, Spain, …). In regards to AI, he has recently published a book : ‘Le RGPD face aux défis de l’intelligence artificielle’ ( Cahier du CRIDS n°49,Larcier 2020) and several articles on ‘AI and Ethics’. 

He has carried out extensive research for the European Union and the Council of Europe, in particular in the areas of data protection, freedom of expression, Internet governance and intellectual property. For the Council of Europe, we note among others, three reports intended for recommendations in matters of telecommunications, Internet and profiling (writing of reports and recommendations on profiling of 2010 and report for a new recommendation on the same theme in 2019). For the European Commission, he is the main author of the report on the concept of adequacy in cross-border flows and data protection (1998), he carried out for the Commission the analysis of the adequacy of many countries ( US, Switzerland, Australia, Japan,…) (latest in 2010).

Yves Poullet was Dean of the Law Faculty of Namur from 1989 to 1996 and from 2000 to 2006, he was appointed Rector of UNamur from 2010 to 2017 before being appointed Professor Emeritus of UNamur. In 2017, he was appointed associate professor at the Catholic University of Lille. He set up and chaired the Doctoral Commission of the law faculties of UCL, St LOUIS and UNamur from 2004 to 2008. He has taught at the Universities of Fordham (US), Sao Pablo (Madrid), Torino, the Balearic Islands, Ouagadougou (Burkina Faso) and Montreal (Canada).
data.short_bio: Yves Poullet was a full professor at the Faculty of Law of UNamur (1982-2017) and associate professor at the University of Liège (Ulg) (2000-2012). He has taught subjects such as new technology law, internet regulation, protection of freedoms, comparative law, Roman law, commercial law, and Sources and Principles of Law. Poullet was also the director of CRIDS since its creation in 1979 until August 31, 2010, where he supervised research in the field of new technologies, more particularly in the areas of privacy, freedoms and the information society, the Internet and the governance.
